questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Determinant of a Block Diagonal or Block Triangular Matrix
questions.problem: Find $\,|\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & a & b & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 5\end{aligned}|$ given that $\,|\begin{aligned}a & b \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}|=8.$
questions.worked_solution:
Notice that we have a block upper triangular matrix. Therefore, its determinant is equal to the product of the diagonal blocks' determinants:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & a & b & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 5\end{aligned}| & =|\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & a & b & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =2\cdot |\begin{aligned}a & b \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}|\cdot 5 \\  & =2\cdot 8\cdot 5 \\  & =80.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Find 
$|\begin{aligned}-3 & b & 0 \\ d & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -4\end{aligned}|$
given that 
$|\begin{aligned}-3 & b \\ d & 2\end{aligned}|=-7.$
questions.worked_solution:
Notice that we have a block diagonal matrix. Therefore, its determinant is equal to the product of the diagonal blocks' determinants:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}-3 & b & 0 \\ d & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -4\end{aligned}| & =|\begin{aligned}-3 & b & 0 \\ d & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -4\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-3 & b \\ d & 2\end{aligned}|\cdot (-4) \\  & =(-7)\cdot (-4) \\  & =28.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Identifying Block Diagonal and Block Triangular Matrices
questions.problem:
Which of the following matrices are block upper triangular?

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 9 & -2\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}3 & 8 & 9 \\ 0 & -1 & 3 \\ 4 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 5 \\ 4 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
A block upper triangular matrix can be partitioned so that it has only square blocks on the main diagonal, and the blocks below the main diagonal contain only zeros.

With that in mind, let's examine our matrices.

- $A$is *not* a block upper triangular matrix since it can't be partitioned in the way described above:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 9 & -2\end{aligned}]
$$

- $B$ is *not* a block upper triangular matrix since it can't be partitioned in the way described above:

$$
\begin{aligned}B=[\begin{aligned}3 & 8 & 9 \\ 0 & -1 & 3 \\ 4 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}3 & 8 & 9 \\ 0 & -1 & 3 \\ 4 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}3 & 8 & 9 \\ 0 & -1 & 3 \\ 4 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

- $C$ is a block upper triangular matrix. Indeed, we can partition it as follows:

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 5 \\ 4 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "$C$ only."

questions.knowledge_point: Identifying Block Diagonal and Block Triangular Matrices
questions.problem:
Which of the following matrices are block diagonal?

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}5 & 2 \\ 7 & 0\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 5\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
A block diagonal matrix can be partitioned so that it has only square blocks on the main diagonal, and all the other blocks contain only zeros.

With that in mind, let's examine our matrices.

- $A$ is a block diagonal matrix. Indeed, we can partition it as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

- $B$ is *not* a block diagonal matrix since it can't be partitioned in the way described above:

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}5 & 2 \\ 7 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

- $C$ is a block diagonal matrix. Indeed, we can partition it as follows:

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 5\end{aligned}]
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "$A$ and $C$ only."

questions.problem: Find $\,|\begin{aligned}p & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 5 & q & 5 & 0 \\ 8 & 0 & 3 & 0 \\ r & 0 & 0 & \frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}|$ given that $\,|\begin{aligned}p & 2 & 0 \\ 5 & q & 5 \\ 8 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}|=12.$
questions.worked_solution:
Notice that we have  a block lower triangular matrix. Therefore, its determinant is equal to the product of the diagonal blocks' determinants:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}p & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 5 & q & 5 & 0 \\ 8 & 0 & 3 & 0 \\ r & 0 & 0 & \frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}| & =|\begin{aligned}p & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 5 & q & 5 & 0 \\ 8 & 0 & 3 & 0 \\ r & 0 & 0 & \frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}p & 2 & 0 \\ 5 & q & 5 \\ 8 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}|\cdot \frac{2}{3} \\  & =12\cdot \frac{2}{3} \\  & =8.\end{aligned}
$$
